title: If Ice Sank, Lakes Could Freeze Solid
narration_text: If ice sank, lakes could freeze from the bottom up. But water breaks the usual rule. When it freezes, its molecules lock into an open crystal structure, taking up more space. That makes ice less dense, so it floats. The floating layer then insulates the liquid water below, helping lake life survive winter.
